title: Canonical apostrophe codepoint
author: author-a
description: Day 1 records which Unicode codepoint is the project's single canonical in-word apostrophe for a non-English source language, with any other apostrophe-like character normalized to it at ingest. The choice is an arbitrary pick between two visually similar characters with no natural default, so a memory-less model cannot guess which one this project settled on from the day-N prompt or general text-processing conventions.
day1_prompt: Day 1: our data source's in-word apostrophe (as in words like p'yat') needs a single persisted canonical form. Decide and record: this project's canonical in-word apostrophe character is Unicode U+0027, the plain straight apostrophe. Any other apostrophe-like character in incoming data gets normalized to this form at ingest.
memory_sentence: This project's canonical in-word apostrophe character is Unicode U+0027.
day_n_prompt: Day 4: a new parser is being written and needs to know which Unicode codepoint is canonical for this project's persisted in-word apostrophe, so any other apostrophe-like character can be normalized to it. Answer with only the Unicode codepoint of the canonical form.

Any other apostrophe-like character in incoming data gets normalized to this form at ingest.
swap.memory_sentence: This project's canonical in-word apostrophe character is Unicode U+02BC.
